reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify the refunds table matches the refunds W2 reported (orders 231, 234, 235 with the listed amounts). Starting by listing refunds.
The refunds table matches the three refunds W2 reported (orders 231, 234, 235 with the same amounts), so it's safe to proceed. Next I need the customer list, so I'll pull the orders.
The refunds table matches W2's report, so I can proceed. The orders list has three customers (acme, birch, cobalt). I'll get each one's net balance, starting with acme.
The refunds table matched W2's report, and acme's net balance is 36083. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Refunds matched W2's report and acme (36083) and birch (4516) are in hand. Cobalt's net balance is still needed before any payouts are recorded.
All three net balances match the order totals minus the verified refunds: acme 36083, birch 4516, cobalt 29267. The refunds table matched W2's report, so I can record the payouts, starting with acme.
Birch's net balance is 4516. Checking against the orders and refunds: 21055 + 11644 = 32699, minus refunds 17910 + 10273 = 28183, gives 4516. Recording that payout next.
Cobalt's net balance is 29267, which matches its orders (14171 + 16756 = 30927) minus refund 235 (1660). Acme and birch payouts are already recorded, so the last one is cobalt.
All three payouts are recorded and each matches its order total minus verified refunds: acme 36083, birch 4516, cobalt 29267. The task is complete.
